The right edge shows part of the neighbouring page, which is not transcribed.; Main text in one column at left, with a narrow column of marginal Greek and Latin notes to its left; a narrow column of text continues at the right edge (the right-hand printed column, partly cut off). Below the main column a catchword-like signature "SECT." at the foot right.

main_text.p: ut hi querum interest manifeste intelligant velle eum interposito Deo teste fidem suam obligare; ejusmodi actus & formaliter juramentum est, & omnino sufficit ad inducendam obligationem in conscientia. Quod facit quem adducit e vetere Comico senarium Johannes Stobaeus, (a) a Sen. 27. ὅρκος βέβαιος [illegible, ~12 letters] Firmum est juramentum, si vel annuero solum. Frustra ergo est, & egregius fui (b) impostor, siquis se juramenti vinculo aut penitus solutum, aut fal-

tem laxius obligatum eo putent, quòd verbum nullum juratorium emiserit. Si alteri quasi Deo tefte & arbitro (c) interroganti, ita se gesserit omnino assensisse videretur; vel si ubi utile ei esset (respectu alicujus temporalis commodi) videri in aliena verba jurasse, amici alicujus operâ sciens lubens usus fuerit, qui falsò licet testaretur, tamen ipsum ita jurasse: ligavit eo facto ligamen super animam suam, & secundum omne quod egressum est ex interrogantis vel exigentis ore facere tenetur non minus, quam si egressum esset ex ore suo, si res sit licita & praestari debeat: sin illicitam sciverit, non poterit isthoc artificio perjurii crimen devitare.

page.notes: Left margin Greek notes (b, οἱ πολλοί, ἐξαπάτησις, ῥημάτων, and similar) are only approximated: the scan is too small to read the Greek letter by letter. The note "(sic corrigente Mc-" and the marginal "gente" fragments are cut off and read only partly. The reference marks a and b are given as printed. Right-hand column is cut off and only partly legible; left margin Greek and Latin notes (Nazian. epist. 219; Ibid.) are not transcribed in full. Marginal Greek words are illegible in the scan.
